# NOTES: Two books in the prompt (BOOK 1 and BOOK 2). Keep separate.

## BOOK 1: "The Clock Struck One" by Fergus Hume (1898, Frederick Warne; Gutenberg 55689)

**Contents:** I Diana on a Bicycle; II The Strange Behaviour of Dr. Scott; III To Every Man His Own Fear; IV More Mysteries; V Mr. Edermont's High Spirits; VI What Happened in the Night; VII A Nine Days' Scandal; VIII The Will of Julian Edermont; IX An Amazing Reward; X Dr. Scott is Still Obstinate; XI Preparing the Ground; XII A Terrible Accusation; XIII Denial; XIV What Dr. Scott Saw; XV The Pearl Brooch; XVI Dora is Startled; XVII A Story of the Past; XVIII Pallant Makes a Statement; XIX More Mysteries; XX The Sins of the Father; XXI So Near, and Yet So Far; XXII What Dora Discovered; XXIII The Madness of Lambert Joad; XXIV The Stolen Manuscript; XXV Confession; XXVI A Final Surprise.

**Characters:**
- Dora Carew: heroine, ~21, tall, sunburnt, gold hair, gray eyes, rides bicycle, "modern Diana." Ward of Edermont; believed £500/yr income (false). Real daughter of Julian Dargill and Laura.
- Dr. Allen Scott: Dora's fiancé, young doctor in Canterbury, son of Dr. Scott (shot dead ~20 yrs earlier). Housekeeper Mrs. Tice raised him. Lodges at green-doored house near Cathedral.
- Julian Edermont (alias of Julian Dargill): recluse at the Red House, Chillum, near Canterbury; small, white hair, beard; fears violent death, prays Litany "From battle and murder, and from sudden death, good Lord, deliver us." Murdered with Zulu knobkerrie, skull smashed, ~1 a.m., 2–3 Aug.
- Lambert Joad: ~60, Edermont's disreputable friend/hanger-on, unsuccessful Anglican parson, drinker (brandy flask), lusts after Dora; sleeps in cottage across road from 9 p.m.
- Meg Gance: cook/general servant.
- Lady Laura Burville (née Treherne; "L.B." pearl brooch): Dora's mother; guest at Hernwood Hall (Sir Harry Hernwood). Husband Sir John Burville, African millionaire. Address 22 Jersey Place, Mayfair.
- Augustus Pallant: red-haired, blue-eyed blackmailer; told Edermont Carew was dead (relieving fear); blackmailed Laura; later shot in San Francisco gambling shop.
- Captain George Theophilus Carew: Dora's real father (sea captain, violent temper), killed Dr. Scott by mistake (1st shot at Dargill), died San Francisco.
- Mr. Carver: lawyer, Canterbury/Mercery Lane, bachelor, "misogamist."
- Inspector Jedd: Canterbury inspector, "tramp" theory.
- Mr. Pride: chubby schoolmaster at Chillum = John Mallison, real killer.
- Dr. Chambers, Dr. Matthewson-type coroner witnesses (Dr. Chambers gave medical evidence).
- Mrs. Shannon/Mrs. Plant not in Book 1.

**Key events:**
- Ch I: Dora meets Allen at bridge 2 miles from Canterbury; Edermont ill after fainting at Chillum Church Litany on seeing Lady Burville.
- Ch II: Joad admits them; Edermont shouts from window "Lambert! ... He will kill me." Allen flees.
- Ch III: Edermont tells Dora her parents "sinned"; Dora's premonition. Joad: "Allen Scott will never marry you."
- Ch IV: Mrs. Tice reveals nothing but photo of Edermont (clean-shaven young).
- Ch V: Pallant visits Edermont ("nightmare is at an end"). Edermont faints.
- Ch VI: Edermont letters to Allen posted; 2 Aug night; cry for help heard ~1 a.m.; Meg finds body 3 Aug morning.
- Ch VII–VIII: Inquest verdict "murdered by persons unknown"; will leaves Red House to Dora, £50,000 to whoever punishes assassin; Dora's supposed £8,000 is fiction.
- Ch XII: Joad accuses Allen (saw him at midnight by moonlight); demands Dora marry him in a week.
- Ch XIII–XIV: Allen's "I was mad that night"; shows letter; brooch found with "L.B." pearls.
- Ch XVI–XVII: Laura reveals she is Dora's mother; Dargill/Edermont was her second husband; Carew her first.
- Ch XX: Mrs. Tice tells Dr. Scott shot by Carew (mistaken for Dargill) at Christchurch.
- Ch XXII–XXIII: Dora finds Edermont's "Confession" in Joad's fireplace; altered hall clock (Meg: clock an hour fast) proves Joad was at house.
- Ch XXIV–XXV: Manuscript: Dora is Dargill's daughter, not Carew's; Allen and Dora may marry. Carver: Joad told him; Pallant and Carew.
- Ch XXV reveal: Mallison (Pride) killed Edermont with knobkerrie after quarrel over stopped pension; Joad hid manuscript; Joad died of heart disease on arrest night; Mallison hanged after confession. Pallant shot in San Francisco. Joad's £50,000 bequeathed to Dora, who with Allen plans spring marriage, Canterbury home, Mrs. Tice housekeeper.

## BOOK 2: "The Layton Court Mystery" by Anthony Berkeley (1926; Gutenberg 72883)

**Contents:** I Eight o'Clock in the Morning; II An Interrupted Breakfast; III Mr. Sheringham is Puzzled; IV Major Jefferson is Reluctant; V Mr. Sheringham Asks a Question; VI Four People Behave Remarkably; VII The Vase That Wasn't; VIII Mr. Sheringham Becomes Startling; IX Mr. Sheringham Sees Visions; X Mrs. Plant is Apprehensive; XI Lady Stanworth Exchanges Glances; XII Hidden Chambers and What-Nots; XIII Mr. Sheringham Investigates a Footprint; XIV Dirty Work at the Ash Pit; XV Mr. Sheringham Amuses an Ancient Rustic; XVI Mr. Sheringham Lectures on Neo-Platonism; XVII Mr. Grierson Becomes Heated; XVIII What the Settee Had to Tell; XIX Mr. Sheringham Loses and Wins the Same Bet; XX Mrs. Plant Proves Disappointing; XXI Mr. Sheringham is Dramatic; XXII Mr. Sheringham Solves the Mystery; XXIII Mrs. Plant Talks; XXIV Mr. Sheringham is Disconcerted; XXV The Mystery Finally Refuses to Accept Mr. Sheringham's Solution; XXVI Mr. Grierson Tries His Hand; XXVII Mr. Sheringham Hits the Mark; XXVIII What Really Did Happen.
Dedication: "To my Father." Preface on detective-fiction fair play.

**Characters:**
- Roger Sheringham: detective-novelist narrator-sleuth, stocky, round face, gray eyes, short pipe, Norfolk jacket, gray flannel trousers; Winchester & Oxford; golf half-blue.
- Alexander "Alec" Grierson: big, broad-shouldered, Scottish-type, Oxford cricketer, engaged to Barbara Shannon on day 1; Roger's friend; plays "Watson."
- Barbara Shannon: ~19, small, fair, gray eyes, firm chin; daughter of Mrs. Shannon (doll-like, peevish).
- Victor Stanworth: host, ~60, genial, City financier, rented Layton Court (Jacobean, Hertfordshire); found dead in library, shot in forehead, 2 a.m. (Dr. Matthewson).
- Lady Stanworth (Lady Cynthia, née Anglemere, dau. of Earl of Grassingham): sister-in-law/hostess, tall, graying; secretly married to Jefferson ~6 months earlier.
- Major Jefferson (Harry): tall, sallow, taciturn ex-army secretary; forced to resign after forging check for friend; blackmailed by Stanworth.
- Graves (Bill Higgins): butler, ex-prize-fighter, blackmailed by Stanworth.
- Mrs. Mary Plant: dark-haired, ~26, husband in Soudan Civil Service; blackmailed by Stanworth (past affair); jewels "Parfum Jasmine" scent.
- Inspector Mansfield, Elchester police; Constable Rudgeman.
- William (gardener), Mrs. William (lodge keeper); Chapman (chauffeur); Alice, Mary (maids); Emma.
- Prince John (Wetherby's farm worker, not actually involved); landlord of village pub.

**Key events (Book 2):**
- Ch I: Roger chats with William, meets Alec; Alec posted letter to bookmaker; Alec's engagement to Barbara broken by her that morning.
- Ch II: Breakfast; Stanworth shot in library; Lady Stanworth announces; Jefferson & Graves break door in.
- Ch III: Body in chair, revolver in right hand; typewritten suicide note "For reasons that concern only myself, I have decided to kill myself," signed "Victor Stanworth" (earlier "Vic" false start). Mrs. Plant seen at safe.
- Ch IV–V: Inspector Mansfield; safe to be opened; Jefferson reluctant; Roger notes ashes in grate.
- Ch VI–VII: Roger deduces wound position awkward; vase on chimney-piece missing one (ring in dust); broken vase.
- Ch VIII–X: Second bullet in panelling behind pillar; Roger theorizes murder; confession fake (pen flooding, second sheet in basket); Mrs. Plant's jewels.
- Ch XI: Safe opened; cash £4,000+; Lady Stanworth's agitation; jewels returned to Mrs. Plant.
- Ch XII–XIII: Secret-door search; footprint under window; window handle trick; footprints in bed.
- Ch XIV–XV: Ash pit; torn pencil note "that brute Prince... this neighbourhood... serious danger"; William's wife warns of John Prince; landlord; bull chase.
- Ch XVI–XVIII: Neo-Platonism lecture; William saw large man 8:30 pm; footprints disappeared; settee powder and long fair hair; Barbara hid there.
- Ch XIX–XXI: Stanworth's bank passbooks show cash payments → blackmail; Jefferson lies about Lady Stanworth (ruled out).
- Ch XXII–XXIV: Roger's theory Jefferson; Mrs. Plant's confession (Stanworth wanted £250; she hadn't it); letter posted from village after death; Lady Stanworth & Jefferson married secretly.
- Ch XXVI–XXVIII: Roger realises hair belonged to Barbara; Alec confesses he killed Stanworth in self-defence after seeing Barbara blackmailed (Stanworth demanded she marry Alec or Mrs. Shannon's secret exposed). Alec burnt documents, faked suicide, typed letters; Roger tells him not to tell Barbara.
